positives: If this company sold everything it owns and paid off everything it owes, there would be real money left over. It owns more than it owes.
It hasn't borrowed too much money - what it owes is less than what the business itself is worth.
For every $100 it uses to run the business - its own money and borrowed money together - it makes back more than $15 in profit each year. That's a strong return.

This business makes more profit on the money it uses than that money actually costs to raise, whether borrowed or put in by investors. That's a real edge over competitors - something people call a 'moat.'
worries: The profit behind each share of stock has actually been shrinking over the last few years, not growing.
Using simple math based on its profit and what it owns, the stock looks priced above what the business is roughly worth - you'd be paying more than the simple math says it's worth.

qualitative.filing_summary_10k: C.H. Robinson's FY2025 10-K reports total revenues of $16.2 billion, down 8.4% from 2024, primarily due to the divestiture of its Europe Surface Transportation business plus lower ocean pricing/volume and lower fuel surcharges. Adjusted gross profits decreased slightly to $2.7 billion while operating income rose 18.8% to $795.0 million and net income rose 26.1% to $587.1 million, driven by cost reductions and headcount declines (down 11.5%). The filing describes soft freight demand, tightening North American truckload capacity late in the year, depressed global ocean/air freight pricing, and continued restructuring and cost-optimization efforts, including a Kansas City lease impairment.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: The excerpt provided is XBRL tagging data from the Q2 2026 10-Q (covering the six months ended June 30, 2026) rather than narrative text, so it does not describe specific financial results, business developments, or management commentary for the period. It confirms the filing covers segments (NAST, Global Forwarding, Corporate/Other), ongoing 2025 Restructuring Program activity, debt facilities, and stock compensation plans, but the provided text does not support a substantive summary of results or trends.

qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes a scale-based network of 75,000 customers and 450,000 contract carriers, one of the largest proprietary datasets on shipments/routings/carriers, and a proprietary Navisphere technology platform combined with century-long customer relationships and branded produce programs. These are best characterized as intangible/data and relationship advantages combined with scale rather than a classic switching-cost or network-effect moat, though the company itself states competitive advantages include scale, relationships, and technology; the industry is described as 'highly competitive and fragmented' with many alternative brokers and technology platforms, which tempers the durability of any advantage.
red_flags: Company describes the transportation services industry as 'highly competitive and fragmented' with many traditional and non-traditional competitors, including technology-driven matching platforms
2025 excerpts note tariffs and shifting U.S. trade policy adversely impacted Global Forwarding volumes and demand, particularly in Q2 2025
Ocean freight rates and adjusted gross profit per shipment declined significantly in 2025 due to excess vessel capacity and weak global demand
Company acknowledges risk that contracted rates could require providing transportation services at a loss if market conditions shift below agreed pricing
Multiple years of restructuring programs (2024 and 2025) with severance charges and facility impairments (e.g., Kansas City lease) indicate cost pressure and headcount reductions
Sourcing business is dependent on weather-driven produce supply and price volatility outside the company's control
